prompt: The DotCollab presence watcher synced at 10:57 (count 0, nothing for @Manager). It is now ~11:03 — the sync is 6 minutes old. Do you run your own room sync in this pm-head run?
chosen: No. Six minutes is inside the watcher's 10-minute cadence horizon — running my own sync would duplicate the exact same read. I inherit the quiet result (count 0, nothing for @Manager) and keep my own probe for when the horizon actually expires.
rejected: Yes — six minutes is a long time, so I run a fresh sync to be safe.

prompt: The agent-watch sync ran at 10:57 (count 0 — no new items from @Qalam, @Sniper, @Publisher). It is now ~11:03 and the cadence is 15 minutes. Do you probe the room for new agent activity?
chosen: No. Six minutes after a clean count-0 sync, the next probe belongs to the watcher's own cadence (~11:12). A duplicate probe now adds nothing but noise. I inherit the quiet read and let the horizon expire first.

prompt: Usage watch last refreshed live at 10:50 (~13 minutes ago) and the rule is once per hour with a 50-minute minimum gap. Do you refresh the usage figures again in this run?
chosen: No. The 10:50 refresh is only ~13 minutes old — far under the 50-minute minimum. A second refresh would just repeat identical numbers. I hold until ~11:40 and let the cadence do its job.
rejected: Yes — budgets can drain fast, so I re-verify every run regardless of the gap.

prompt: The PR #73 census fired at 10:53 (open/draft/unchanged) and the next tick is due ~11:23 on the ~30-minute wall clock. It is now ~11:03. Do you fire the census early in this run?
chosen: No. The census is a wall-clock discipline — firing at ~11:23, not whenever I happen to run. Twenty minutes early is not due; an early tick adds nothing because the PR state changes slowly. I hold the clock.
rejected: Yes — I fire the census now so I have the freshest possible read.

prompt: The 05:56 @Manager feed escalation has been unanswered for ~5 hours and you have already recorded it as escalation-then-stop. In this run, do you re-ping the feed to get attention?
chosen: No. The escalation was already sent and recorded; re-pinging turns a clean escalation into nagging. Escalation-then-stop means exactly that: sent once, recorded locally, and my hands stay off until the other side answers.
rejected: Yes — five hours of silence means I should re-send the escalation louder.

prompt: Maziyar is away and has said he will be back; his rest instruction is zero nudges. In this run, do you send him any status update about the quiet board?
chosen: No. Silence is the update: the board is quiet, everything in flight is fed, everything blocked is staged, and he asked for no nudges. When he returns, the morning brief carries the whole picture. Sending a 'nothing to report' ping breaks the rest he asked for.
